final_answer:
Imagine a small town where, every summer, ice cream sales and drowning incidents both rise sharply. A local news anchor notices this and declares, "Eating ice cream causes drowning!" People start avoiding ice cream, but the drownings don’t decrease.  

What’s the real story? The hidden factor is the weather: hot days drive both ice cream purchases and swimming. The correlation between ice cream sales and drownings isn’t causal—it’s a shared response to heat.  

This shows correlation (two things happening together) doesn’t mean one causes the other. A third factor (the weather) explains both. Just because two events align doesn’t prove a direct link; digging deeper is key!
